key_insight: Suicide-related clinical dialogue forms a therapist-centered, hub-and-spoke network where higher-severity content becomes increasingly peripheral and active suicidal ideation often bridges toward method, plan, and attempt talk.
clinical_relevance: Mapping how suicide topics flow across turns could help clinicians and decision-support tools spot escalation patterns earlier during psychotherapy conversations.
method: 110 psychotherapy sessions from SPEAK-SAFE were transcribed and suicidality-relevant utterances were classified with Qwen3-32B using an adapted C-SSRS schema.
The suicide-related utterances were converted into a weighted directed category-transition network.
Network metrics including centrality, reciprocity, clustering, assortativity, and path length were analyzed.
evidence_signal: Human expert review of a 30-session subsample showed substantial agreement with the LLM labels (Spearman rho = 0.885; ICC[2,1] = 0.708).
watch_item: This is a cross-sectional proof-of-concept from psychotherapy transcripts, so the network patterns may not generalize to other settings, languages, or real-time clinical use without further validation.
paper_title: From Symptom Networks to Conversation Networks: A Cross-Sectional Study Mapping the Topology of Suicide-Related Clinical Dialogue
